pattern: The six dates are the Monday and Tuesday run dates of the window, and they share one signature. On every Monday and Tuesday run date from 2026-09-14 to 2026-10-13 (ten dates) the first version of that day's forwardfill_v2/transactions file is header-only (4354 to 4358 bytes, zero data rows); on every other run date in that span the first version carries rows (1.0 to 36.6 MB). The runner emits the bronze sentinel only when every table is complete. The runner revision deployed before 2026-10-07T00:50:44Z (the parent of commit 3709ae40d6, read by git show) called the shared emit_bronze_sentinel, which withheld the sentinel on the header-only transactions (WARN not content-complete, logged 2026-10-05 and 2026-10-06), then printed OK bronze sentinel emitted unconditionally (parent lines 206-207). S3 holds no sentinel object for any of the six dates. With no sentinel the S3 event never reaches bd-silver-merge, so bd-price-update is not invoked and no silver/prices/<date>.parquet is written. The header-only partitions were re-landed with rows three days later, but nothing re-emits a sentinel for a past run date. The schedule is not the cause: bd-49f-session-daily (cron(0 0 * * ? *), ENABLED) starts the chain every day, and the mode marker was written on all six dates. The revision deployed on 2026-10-07 (commit 3709ae40d6, deployed bytes md5 968b33e2e14b0a1e0416445c7da19d98, equal to the repo file) accepts a measured-empty transactions window; sentinels exist again for 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-13, both header-only on first landing. Four of the six dates (2026-09-21, 09-22, 09-28, 09-29) are NOT_DETERMINED from logs because the log retention has ended; the S3 signature is the same as for the two readable dates.
